To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
user-level IPC is a viable solution that can provide a performance boost over kernel-level IPC and that user-level device drivers are a viable solution to reduce kernel context switching.

(1) user level communication and device driver support can be implemented in a manner that is more efficient than kernel level support, and (2) the performance of user level IPC and device driver support are comparable to kernel level implementations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a high performance, user level, operating system.
the implementation of user level communication services and device drivers in a modern operating system kernel.
the development of a kernel that provides high performance IPC and device management services to applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Raven kernel is an operating system that provides a complete set of operating system services to a user application.
the Raven kernel is a highly scalable, low overhead, user level operating system kernel.
the Raven kernel has been designed to minimize kernel intervention for many low level operating system tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have implemented the Raven kernel to support user level send/receives and user level device drivers.
the Raven kernel provides a user level interface for IPC and device drivers.
we have reduced kernel intervention for many services by an order of magnitude or better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
user level implementations can be very effective at reducing kernel intervention and increasing performance.
a kernel does not have to be monolithic.
a user level implementation of a kernel service is often more efficient than the traditional kernel implementation of the same service.
